feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=a+\lambda b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $a.$ So, we begin with the vector $a,$ and then find the remaining vector needed to reach the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931259/assets/45a4735bf7710ff7c2699a9b42b10c34807d6162a3d7da38842ba87f13158788.png)

Note that in $△OAC,$ we have:

- $AC=\frac{1}{2}|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $b$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=\frac{1}{2}b.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =a+\frac{1}{2}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=a+\lambda b=a+\frac{1}{2}b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $b,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{1}{2}
$$
